questions.prompt: Match the question to the chart: trend over time → ? · contribution ranking → ? · relationship of two measures → ? · single value per region/segment cell → ?
options: Line · sorted bar (+ % of total) · scatter · highlight/heat table
questions.explain: The exam gives a BUSINESS question; you pick the standard encoding: time → **line**, ranking → **sorted bars**, two measures → **scatter**, matrix of one aggregate → **heat map** (Color on Marks). Box plot when DISTRIBUTION (median/quartiles/outliers) matters.

options: Dimensions = categorical fields that slice the view (blue); measures = numeric fields that get aggregated (green)
They are interchangeable labels with no effect
questions.explain: **Dimensions slice, measures aggregate** — the core mental model. Blue/green also encodes discrete/continuous, which controls headers vs axes.

questions.source: Gate — table calc vs calculated field
questions.prompt: Percent-of-total via Quick Table Calculation vs a calculated field — the difference:
options: Table calc transforms the AGGREGATED result in the view; a calculated field creates a real new field usable anywhere
They are identical in every way
Table calcs change the source data
questions.explain: **Table calcs** (Percent of Total, Running Sum…) post-process the view's aggregates. **Calculated fields** (e.g., Margin = SUM(Profit)/SUM(Sales), shown as AGG) become reusable fields in the Data pane.

questions.prompt: One Category filter must drive ALL sheets (different data sources) on a dashboard:
options: Filter card caret → Apply to Worksheets → All Using Related Data Sources
Copy the filter to each sheet manually every time
Filters only work on one sheet
questions.explain: **Apply to Worksheets → All Using Related Data Sources** = the global-filter move (Challenge S3.10c). Clicking a Category value then filters map + line + scatter simultaneously.

options: Dashboard = one interactive screen of multiple sheets; Story = a sequence of captioned points (dashboards/sheets) that narrate insights
questions.explain: **Story points** carry navigator captions ('the takeaway sentence') — the narrative layer. Export everything with **File → Export Packaged Workbook (.twbx)**.

questions.prompt: To count customers who purchased in BOTH 2017 and 2018:
options: Create a set per year → Combined Set ('Shared members in both sets') → filter + COUNTD(Customer Name)
questions.explain: OR-filtering counts EITHER year; the **combined set's intersection** counts BOTH. COUNTD = distinct customers. Lecture answer: **605**.

questions.prompt: On a filled map with Profit → Color (diverging) and Sales → Size, the biggest-loss state is found by:
options: The darkest color at the negative end of the diverging palette (hover to confirm the value)
questions.explain: **Color = profit** (the diverging palette's negative extreme), **size = sales** — two channels, two questions. Hover for the tooltip's exact number before answering.

questions.prompt: Tableau's forecast band represents the prediction interval at what default confidence percentage? (number)
questions.explain: **95%** by default. Horizon: right-click forecast → Forecast Options → 'Exactly N months'. Trend lines: hover shows equation, R², p-value.
